messages:
Maya P (PM): Quick heads-up — execs want a short "one-pager" for launch that explains why some features are MVP vs v1. We need decisions today: do we keep a hard cut or adopt a toggle/playbook approach for heavy infra items?

Ian G (Eng): Toggle/playbook reduces risk. We can ship toggles for quantization and global cache, default off for public tenants, on for pilot tenants. That avoids infra migrations impacting everyone.

Zoe L (Eng-ML): Toggle is ok but model quality regressions must be gated. We need a regression harness (small test set) and an auto-rollback if outputs shift too much. That's MVP work but scoped.

Hector V (ProdOps): Ops caution: toggles require control-plane flags + telemetry hooks. If we flip accidentally we could overload GPUs. Need safe defaults and a throttling gate. ~2 days infra ops work.

Maya P (PM): Tradeoff: hard cut (simpler messaging, more upfront deferrals) vs toggle (flexible demos, more ops). Which minimizes overall timeline risk for the milestone?

Ian G (Eng): Timeline risk: toggle adds ~2–3d infra + 1d engineering to wire flags. But it allows pilots and demos to look production-grade. Hard cut is fastest to ship but forces bigger v1 scope.

Rae J (Customer): From customer side — pilots want to see the optimized experience. If toggle lets our pilot tenants opt in safely, that's preferable. They'll accept pilot badges and capacity limits.

Zoe L (Eng-ML): For safety add a metric that monitors output drift and tail latency. If drift >5% or 95th latency > threshold, auto-disable toggle for that tenant. We can mock the UI metric in demo.

Hector V (ProdOps): I'll scope the gating policy: tenant token-bucket + auto-disable hook + alert. I'll need Contingency Runbook entry in the deploy doc.

Maya P (PM): Decision: go with toggle/playbook approach for heavy infra (global cache, quantized kernels). MVP will ship toggles turned off for public tenants; pilot tenants can opt-in. Acceptance criteria for demo/MVP:
- toggles present and documented (work: Ian)
- regression harness + auto-rollback rule (work: Zoe)
- pilot gating + throttling + runbook (work: Hector)
- customer-facing pilot badge + consent language (work: Rae)

Ian G (Eng): Implementation notes: flag service already exists. I'll add two flags: "quantized.experimental" and "global-cache.pilot". Spike + PR ~2d.

Zoe L (Eng-ML): I'll assemble a 40-sample regression set focused on customer-critical prompts and wire a lightweight fingerprint check. PR in 1.5d.

Hector V (ProdOps): I'll draft the runbook and the throttle config. Need 2d. Will coordinate alert thresholds with Zoe.

Rae J (Customer): I'll prepare the pilot consent copy and sample slide for demos. Will share with PM for approval.

deploy-bot: Reminder: staging deploy for milestone branch 2024-11-04T14:00 UTC.

Maya P (PM): Ok — I'll update the exec one-pager to justify toggles as a lower-risk, demo-friendly approach and mark global embeddings + broader quantization rollout as v1 backlog. Reconvene tomorrow EOD for status. :thumbsup:
